newsitem.title: UK: YEAREND - Bond bulls need new chart highs to feed on.
newsitem.headline: YEAREND - Bond bulls need new chart highs to feed on.

text.p: International bond markets will go into 1997 with the backing of charts but they will quickly have to form new highs to maintain that potential, technical analysts said.
The closing stages of 1996 saw a bond market correction, but analysts said the picture for some markets remains positive.

"BTPs have the most bullish chart I have seen," said Robin Wilkin, senior technical analyst at MCM YieldWatch in London. "Bunds have got a lot to do to recover from their recent sharp failure, which was less harsh for T-bonds.

All along the debt market spectrum, Fibonacci retracement and projection levels dominate in the current thinking for where prices are headed. After large swings in 1996, many chart-gazers are setting targets based on measurements of prior moves.
Analysts said a recent retreat by BTPs could be viewed as consolidation within an overall strong bull-trend on a continuation chart.
March BTP futures traded on LIFFE were down 0.12 at 128.81 at 0845 GMT Tuesday.

"The recent fall was non-existent compared with what this market has done since early 1995," said Wilkin. "It is continuing to make higher highs and higher lows on a weekly basis and there are no impulsive downmoves."
In March 1995, BTP futures were trading around 91.44, and then rose to 106.40 in September the same year.
A 2.618 percent Fibonacci projection of that move, gives a target of 130.50. Above there, 145.43 was the next target.
Analysts said T-bonds are also widely expected to have the strength to challenge historical highs, but opinions differ as to whether they will be as bullish as their Italian cousins.
March T-bond futures were trading at 112-24 at 0845 GMT on Tuesday, and were expected to weaken slightly into the end of the year.
Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank in London, said T-bonds would need to work gradually higher towards 114-00/115-00, starting from 112-00 in early 1997.
The key support level for the contract was around 106-00, analysts said. In 1996, T-bonds set a low of 105-28 on July 8, and later touched 106-00 on September 6.

"The double bottom at 106-00 on continuation charts has set a base for the market," he said. "It can then challenge 120-00/122-00, sometime before the summer (mid-1997)," he said, adding that he did not expect the 122-00 resistance to break.
Some analysts were more bullish on T-bonds, seeing the bull-run from that low of 106-00 as still intact.
"It's basing out at 114-00," said MCM's Wilkin. "There is a good chance that the recent downmove is just a correction before a further push higher."
He saw T-bonds pushing up to 118-20 resistance initially, a 78.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the January-July 1996 fall, before retesting the 122-00 highs.
The 105-28 level was also significant as a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of the rally from a low of 96-01 in November 1994 to the January 1996 high at 122-04.
"It has based out so well at the 62 percent retracement at 105-28 that there is nothing to stop an impulsive move higher," said Wilkin. "We'll see a test of the highs, and then new highs."
If the market forms a base at 112-20, the December 6 low, then projection targets for T-bonds would be 123-17, 130-08 and then the 132-00 area.

However, Celaya said the end of the second quarter and the start of the third quarter will see weakness creeping in to spoil the T-bond party. That downmove will target 110-00, which it must hold to avoid revisiting the 106-00 level seen mid-1996. David Wood, an independent technical analyst based near London, said the downside break would not come until the end of 1997, but had the potential to be quite deep.
A break of 100-00 on the downside would target 95-25, a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of the rally from 122-04 in January down to 105-28 in July.
"The fact that we've had a double top at 122-00 would make a trough at 96-00 quite attractive from a symmetrical point of view," said Wood.

In September 1993 and January 1996, on continuation charts, the T-bond has formed two peaks at 122-10 and 122-04. On an overall basis, Wood advised that mid-March, June, September and December have proved to be critical for the T-bond, and could be watched for signs of a change in trend.
"The T-bond has a propensity to turn around in these three-monthly cycles," said Wood. "Even if it is moving strongly, you can see a turn at these points."
Celaya and Wood said the Bund charts were more bullish than their U.S. counterparts, as they had performed better during the past year.
March Bund futures were at 100.04 by 0845 GMT, compared with 100.20 at the close of the previous session.
"Bunds are still trapped in a bull trend, and are more bullish than the T-bond," said Celaya. "I'd expect to see further probes to the upside."

As Bunds set new all-time highs this year, that adds strength to the upside, technical analysts said. However, the contract must hold above 98.00, in order to retain the upside potential to reach 102.00 and then 104.00.
"If it goes below 98.00 then there will be a sell-off and reversal," said Celaya. "It could go back to the low 94.00 area we saw in June."
On daily continuation charts, Bund futures set a low of 94.36 in mid-June.

However, Wilkin said Bunds' success in setting new all-time highs was tempered by the sharp reversal in early December 1996. To improve the picture, the Bund must break back above 102.00 or 101.36 by the end of 1996.
He cited trendline support at 96.57, drawn from a low of 88.05 on January 6 1995 to the mid-June 1996 low.
"I see Bunds as weaker than T-bonds, judging by the sharpness of the recent drop," said Wilkin.
Japanese government bond (JGB) charts suggest a retest of pivotal resistance at 126.52/65, according to technical analysis from Credit Suisse.
March JGB futures on LIFFE were trading at 125.64.

"A break will target 128.40/50, where the market should stall," a Credit Suisse publication said. "Failure to break 126.65 will suggest a larger bearish pattern is under construction and a decline to 122.54 and then 120.67/50 will be seen."
